method_card.title: Recognising Cubic, Reciprocal & Exponential Graphs
method_card.content:
Cubic graphs \(y = ax^3 + \ldots\) make an S-shape, rising from bottom-left to top-right when \(a > 0\).

Reciprocal graphs \(y = \frac{a}{x}\) have two branches and never touch the axes.

Exponential graphs \(y = a^x\) pass through \((0, 1)\); they grow when \(a > 1\) and decay when \(0 < a < 1\).
method_card.example: Sketch \(y = \frac{6}{x}\). \(x = 1 \to 6\), \(x = 2 \to 3\), \(x = 3 \to 2\), with the mirror branch in quadrant 3 for negative x. Two branches; the curve never meets the axes.
